322962.title: Unimodality conjecture for normalized core-count increments
322962.statement:
Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$, let $c_t(n)$ be the number of $t$-core partitions of $n$, and define

$$
\pi_t(n)=\frac{c_{t+1}(n)-c_t(n)}{p(n)}.
$$

For fixed $n\geq 63$, consider the sequence indexed by $t$ with $4\leq t\leq n-7$. **Unimodality conjecture for normalized core-count increments.** The sequence

$$
\{\pi_t(n)\}_{4\leq t\leq n-7}
$$

is unimodal. This is supported by numerical plots and is stated without a proof.

322964.title: Numerical inequalities for self-conjugate 9-core partitions
322964.statement:
Let $sc_9(n)$ denote the number of self-conjugate $9$-core partitions of $n$, and let $n$ be a non-negative integer. **Numerical inequalities for self-conjugate 9-core partitions.** The following inequalities are conjectured:

1. If $n\geq 49$, then $sc_9(4n)>3\,sc_9(n)$.
2. If $n\geq 1$, then $sc_9(4n+1)>1.9\,sc_9(n)$.
3. If $n\geq 17$, then $sc_9(4n+3)>1.9\,sc_9(n)$.
4. If $n\geq 1$, then $sc_9(4n+4)>2.6\,sc_9(n)$.
These claims are based on experimental data, and the source gives no proof.

323256.title: The 7-torsion conjecture for matching complexes
323256.statement:
Let $n=2k+1+3r$ and $d=k-1+r$, so that the relevant reduced homology group is $\tilde{H}_{k-1+r}(\mathsf{M}_{2k+1+3r};\mathbb{Z})$. **The 7-torsion conjecture.** The group contains elements of order $7$ whenever $r\geq 4$ and $k\geq 2r-3$. Equivalently, $\tilde{H}_d(\mathsf{M}_n;\mathbb{Z})$ contains elements of order $7$ whenever

$$
\frac{3n-13}{7}\leq d\leq\frac{n-7}{2}.
$$

The source notes that the available evidence is limited, so this remains an open conjectural extension of the known cases.

323267.title: Poincaré-polynomial upper-bound conjecture for Rothe diagrams
323267.statement:
Fix a permutation $w\in\mathfrak{S}_n$, and let $R_w$ be its Rothe diagram. Let $\operatorname{inv}(w)$ denote the inversion number of $w$, and let $P_w(q)$ be the Poincaré polynomial associated with $w$. **Poincaré-polynomial Rothe-diagram conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
\frac{\operatorname{mat}_q(n,R_w,n)}{(q-1)^n}
$$

is coefficient-wise less than or equal to

$$
q^{\binom{n}{2}-\operatorname{inv}(w)}P_w(q).
$$

Equality holds if and only if $w$ avoids the patterns $1324$, $24153$, $31524$, and $426153$. Computational evidence was available for $n\leq 7$; the conjecture relates rank enumerators of Rothe diagrams to Poincaré polynomials and remains open in general.

323852.title: Nonexistence conjecture for simple Venn diagrams with dihedral symmetry
323852.statement:
A **simple Venn diagram** is a Venn diagram in which no three curves meet at a point. A symmetric Venn diagram has **dihedral symmetry** if it is left invariant by flipping it over, possibly followed by a rotation.

**Dihedral-symmetry nonexistence conjecture.** There is no simple Venn diagram with dihedral symmetry if $n>3$.

The statement is motivated by the near-dihedral symmetry of the authors' simple symmetric 11-Venn diagram and by a construction with dihedral symmetry that is not simple. Its resolution is not specified in the source.

326023.title: Weight-four P1 class enumeration conjecture
326023.statement:
Let $F_2$ be the free group on two generators. An automorphic conjugacy class is of type (P1) as defined in the paper; its size is the cardinality of its vertex set, and the **weight** of a word $w$ is $\min((a)_w,(b)_w)$, where $(a)_w$ and $(b)_w$ count the occurrences of $a$ and $b$. **Weight-four P1 enumeration conjecture.** For $k\geq 4$ and $n\geq\max(2k-2,9)$, the number of (P1) classes of size $n-k$ whose minimal words have length $n$ and weight $4$ is

$$
\begin{cases}
6k-24 & \text{if } k\equiv 0\pmod 2,\\
6k-25 & \text{if } k\equiv 1\pmod 2.
\end{cases}
$$
 This is one of the paper's conjectural enumeration formulas; the authors state that these conjectures and their generalizations remain open problems.

326116.title: Local dimension conjecture for 24- and 25-point octonionic simplices
326116.statement:
Let ${\mathbb O}{\mathbb P}^2$ be octonionic projective $2$-space, and let the **space of tight simplices** mean the local moduli space of tight simplices, with the stated dimension understood in a neighborhood of the simplex.

**Local dimension conjecture.** There exists a $24$-point, respectively $25$-point, tight simplex in ${\mathbb O}{\mathbb P}^2$ such that, in a neighborhood of it, the space of tight simplices has dimension $56$, respectively $49$.

The corresponding simplices are proved to exist in the paper, while the larger local dimensions are inferred from numerical evidence and remain conjectural.

326284.title: Conforti, Cornuéjols and Vušković's conjecture on balanceable bipartite graphs
326284.statement: A bipartite graph is **balanceable** if its edges can be assigned weights $+1$ or $-1$ so that the resulting signed bipartite graph has every hole's edge-weight sum divisible by four. Let $R_{10}$ be the graph formed from the cycle $x_1x_2\ldots x_{10}x_1$ together with the chords $x_ix_{i+5}$ for $1\leq i\leq 5$. **Conforti, Cornuéjols and Vušković's conjecture.** In a balanceable bipartite graph, either every edge belongs to some $R_{10}$ or there is an edge that is not the unique chord of a cycle. The source presents this as a proposed generalisation of the balanced-graph conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.

326771.title: Aouchiche–Hansen–Cioabă's maximal-energy conjecture for tricyclic graphs
326771.statement:
Let $P_n^{6,6,6}$, for $n\geq 20$, be the graph obtained from three copies of $C_6$ and a path $P_{n-18}$ by adding a single edge between each of two copies of $C_6$ and one endpoint of the path, and a single edge from the third copy of $C_6$ to the other endpoint. **Aouchiche–Hansen–Cioabă's conjecture.** If $G$ is a tricyclic graph on $n$ vertices with $n=20$ or $n\geq 22$, then

$$
\mathcal{E}(G)\leq \mathcal{E}(P_n^{6,6,6})
$$

with equality if and only if $G\cong P_n^{6,6,6}$. The problem of finding tricyclic graphs maximizing energy is described as open, and this conjecture was proposed from AutoGraphiX experiments.

328340.title: The diameter conjecture for divisibility graphs of symmetric and alternating groups
328340.statement: For $n\geq 1$, let $D(S_n)$ and $D(A_n)$ be the divisibility graphs whose vertices correspond to conjugacy classes of $S_n$ and $A_n$, respectively, with adjacency determined by divisibility of conjugacy-class sizes. **Diameter conjecture.** The best upper bound for the diameter of $D(S_n)$ and $D(A_n)$ is $4$. This conjecture sharpens the preceding bounds $\operatorname{diam}(D(S_n))\leq 8$ and $\operatorname{diam}(D(A_n))\leq 10$; the source provides no resolution.

329537.title: The Type BII coefficient-polynomial conjecture
329537.statement:
At $q=1$, write the Type BII sum as 
$$
S_N=\sum_{j=0}^{N}S_{N,j}(Q+Q^{-1})^j.
$$
 **Type BII coefficient-polynomial conjecture.** For the relevant coefficient index $i$, 
$$
S_{N,N-i}=\left(\prod_{j=1}^{i}(2j)^{-1}\right)P_i(N),
$$
 where 
$$
P_i(N)=N^{2i}-iN^{2i-1}+\sum_{k=0}^{2i-2}p_{i,k}N^k,
$$
 with $p_{i,k}\in\mathbb{Z}$. The source reports verification through $j=7$ and $N=20$ and gives initial polynomials, but no proof or resolution is supplied.

329645.title: Alphabet-independence conjecture for the sets R(n,m)
329645.statement:
Let $R(n,m)$ denote the set of numbers of valid plane trees associated with primary sequences having $n$ edges over an alphabet with $m$ complementary letter pairs. The sets $R(n,m)$ are therefore indexed by the number of edges and the alphabet size.

**Alphabet-independence conjecture.** The set $R(n,m)$ depends only on $n$.

The conjecture is supported by computations for $R(n,2)$ with $n\leq 6$, for $R(n,3)$ and $R(n,4)$ with $n\leq 5$, and for $R(n,m)$ with $n\leq 4$ and $m\leq 10$; in all these cases, $R(n,m)$ agrees with $R(n,1)$.

329897.title: The winning-strategy conjecture for Building Nim
329897.statement:
Let $\operatorname{BN}(2n,\ell)$ denote the Building Nim game with parameters $2n$ and $\ell$, and let $\text{P1}$ and $\text{P2}$ be its two players. **Winning-strategy conjecture.** Player $\text{P1}$ wins $\operatorname{BN}(2n,\ell)$ whenever

$$
2n>\ell+3.
$$

Computer explorations suggest this criterion beyond the cases established in the preceding analysis, while the source notes that $\text{P1}$ has a winning strategy for $\operatorname{BN}(10,5)$ and other cases. A general proof is not provided.

330128.title: Characterization of competition graphs induced by 123-avoiding permutations
330128.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph in $C(\mathcal{S}_n)$. An induced subgraph is a subgraph induced by a specified subset of the vertices of $G$.

**123-avoidance conjecture.**

$$
G\in C(\mathcal{S}_n(123))\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad K_{1,3}\text{ is not an induced subgraph of }G.
$$

The proposition preceding this conjecture proves the reverse implication: if $K_{1,3}$ is an induced subgraph of $G$, then $G\notin C(\mathcal{S}_n(123))$ for $n\geq 7$. The conjecture asserts the converse as well, and is presented as the analogue of the theorem characterizing $C(\mathcal{S}_n(132))$ by the absence of an induced $P_3$.

330350.title: Manetti's geography inequality for irregular surfaces
330350.statement:
Let $X$ be a minimal surface of general type and maximal Albanese dimension with irregularity $q\geq 4$. **Manetti's geography conjecture.** One should have

$$
K_X^2\geq 4\chi(\mathcal O_X)+4(q-3).
$$

This inequality concerns how the irregularity constrains the geography of surfaces of general type and maximal Albanese dimension. The source presents it as a conjecture of Manetti and states that it is proved there when $K_X^2\geq 36(q-2)$ or $\chi(\mathcal O_X)\geq 8(q-2)$; the supplied status therefore records it as resolved.

331617.title: Entringer number conjecture for 000-avoiding inversion sequences
331617.statement:
The Entringer numbers $d_{n,k}$ count down/up permutations of $[n+1]$ whose first entry is $k+1$, and satisfy

$$
d_{n,k}=d_{n,k-1}+d_{n-1,n-k}.
$$

An **Entringer number conjecture** asserts that, for $n\geq 1$ and $0\leq k\leq n-1$, $d_{n,k}$ is the number of inversion sequences $e\in\mathbf{I}_n(000)$ with last entry $e_n=k-1$.

This conjecture proposes a direct interpretation of the Entringer numbers in terms of 000-avoiding inversion sequences; the source reports it as suggested by computations, and no resolution is provided.

332319.title: Almkvist's conjecture on the unimodality of Gaussian polynomials
332319.statement:
Let $n$ and $r$ be positive integers, and define

$$
f_{n,r}(q)=\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{1-q^{ri}}{1-q^i}.
$$

**Almkvist's conjecture.** The polynomial $f_{n,r}(q)$ is an ${\rm A}$-polynomial if either $r$ is even and $n\ge 1$, or $r$ is odd and $n\ge 11$.
This conjecture gives sufficient conditions for the Gaussian polynomial to have the coefficient properties encoded by an ${\rm A}$-polynomial. The surrounding discussion attributes it to Almkvist; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

333415.title: Neumann–Lara's 2-colourability conjecture for planar digraphs
333415.statement: Let $D$ be an oriented planar graph, meaning a planar digraph without directed cycles of length at most $2$. A $2$-colouring of $D$ is a function $f:V(D)\to\{1,2\}$ such that the subdigraph induced by the vertices of each colour is acyclic. **Neumann–Lara's conjecture.** Every oriented planar graph is $2$-colourable. The conjecture was proposed by Neumann–Lara in 1985 and independently by Škrekovski. The paper proves the relaxed version for planar digraphs of digirth at least four, while the case of digirth at least three remains open.

334269.title: Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture for power domination
334269.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement. Assume that every component of both $G$ and $\overline{G}$ has order at least $3$. Write $\gamma_P(G)$ for the power domination number of $G$. **Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture for power domination.**

$$
\gamma_P(G)+\gamma_P(\overline{G})\le \left\lfloor\frac{n}{3}\right\rfloor+2.
$$

The bound would show that the exceptional orders $13,14,16,17,20$ arising in the preceding result are not genuine exceptions. The paper notes that no counterexamples are known, while the conjecture remains unresolved.

334721.title: Extremal restraint conjecture for odd cycles
334721.statement:
Let $C_n$ be an odd cycle with vertex set $\{v_1,v_2,\dots,v_n\}$ and edge set

$$
\{v_1v_2,v_2v_3,\dots,v_{n-1}v_n,v_1v_n\}.
$$

For a restraint $r$, write $r\cong r^*$ when $r$ is equivalent to $r^*$. Define $r^*$ on $C_n$ by

$$
r^*(v_i)=\begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } i\in\{1,3,5,\dots,\frac{n-1}{2}\},\\ 2 & \text{if } i\in\{2,4,6,\dots,\frac{n-3}{2}\}\cup\{\frac{n+3}{2},\frac{n+7}{2},\frac{n+11}{2},\dots,n\},\\ 3 & \text{if } i\in\{\frac{n+1}{2},\frac{n+5}{2},\frac{n+9}{2},\dots,n-1\}.\end{cases}
$$

**Extremal restraint conjecture.** If $r\in R_{\operatorname{max}}(C_n,1)$, then $r\cong r^*$.

The preceding examples show that determining $R_{\operatorname{max}}(G,k)$ remains open for odd cycles; this conjecture proposes the extremal restraint for the case $k=1$.
